name: Demon, Xylvarus
body:
Xylvarus Demon
CR 13

This red, sinewy fiend looks through its cunning blue eyes over a set of sharp, needle-like teeth. Its back is covered in sharp, bony appendages and each of its hands ends in a set of three claws, each the length of a shortsword and covered in a soft, violet glow.

XP 25,600
CE Large outsider (chaotic, demon, evil, extraplanar)
Init +7; Senses arcane sight, darkvision, 60 ft., low-light vision, see invisibility; Perception +29

DEFENSE

AC 26, touch 13, flat-footed 22 (+3 Dex, +1 dodge, -1 size, +13 natural)
hp 200 (16d10+112)
Fort +12, Ref +13, Will +12
DR 10/cold iron or good; Immune electricity, fire, poison; Resist acid 10, cold 10; SR 28

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft.
Melee 2 claws +25 (3d6+9/19-20 plus magic drain), bite +25 (1d8+9/19-20 plus grab), tail slap +19 (1d8+4) Space 10 ft.; Reach 10 ft.
Special Attacks rake (4 claws +20, 1d6+4)
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 16th; concentration +19)

Constant—arcane sight, see invisibility
At will—arcane disruption (DC 15), darkness, greater dispel magic, greater teleport (self plus 50 lbs. of objects only)
3/day—feeblemind (DC 18), unholy blight (DC 17)
1/day—mage’s disjunction (DC 22), summon (level 4, 1d3 babau 50%)

STATISTICS

Str 28, Dex 16, Con 25, Int 13, Wis 14, Cha 16
Base Atk +16; CMB +26 (+30 grapple); CMD 40
Feats Combat Reflexes, Dodge, Improved Critical (bite, claw), Improved Initiative, Lunge, Weapon Focus (bite, claw)
Skills Intimidate +22, Knowledge (arcana, planes) +20, Perception +29, Sense Motive +21, Spellcraft +20, Stealth +18; Racial Modifiers +8 Perception
Languages Abyssal, Celestial, Draconic; telepathy 100 ft.

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Magic Drain (Su)

Xylvarus’ claws drain magic from creatures and objects they hit, which has two effects. First, a hit from a xylvarus’ claw also functions as dispel magic (CL 16th). A xylvarus gains temporary hit points equal to 3 times the spell level of the dispelled effect. Those hit points stack up to 50 and last for 1 hour. The second effect affects only creatures capable of casting spells or using spell-like abilities. A struck creature loses its highest-level prepared spell, spell slot, or use of spell-like ability unless it succeeds at a DC 25 Will save. The save DC is Constitution-based.

ECOLOGY

Environment any (Abyss)
Organization solitary, pair
Treasure standard

Xylvari demons form from bloodthirsty witch hunters: people who murdered spellcasters out of fear, hate or prejudice. They are notably similar to babau, with their red skin, lanky builds, surprising strength and affinity for murder. Xylvari are, however, vastly more powerful than their smaller cousins, both physically and accounting for their potent abilities. While a xylvarus can and will tear apart martial opponents in combat, they are specialized in hunting down spellcasters and that’s where they truly thrive. They have a wide array of traits that help them achieve this goal. Their monstrously long, curved claws drain magic with each hit, shattering both spells already present on their targets and pulling the very capacity for magic from their victims, regardless if the spells come from a sorcerer’s instinct or a wizard’s mind. Their own magic is able to thoroughly and permanently destroy the minds of their opponents, with arcane spellcasters being especially vulnerable. Their abilities can unmake even the strongest of magic, and as such xylvari are sometimes forced against their will by more powerful demons to attempt destruction of various artifacts of good. Adding to that, every xylvarus is abnormally resistant to magic itself, even by demon standards, and their intensely blue eyes distinguish between auras as easily as a human eye distinguishes between colors, both valuable abilities on their home plane.

Although, being demons, xylvari don’t need to eat, the act of draining magic with their claws is akin to feeding and it both elates and empowers them to do so. While this is incredibly satisfying, a xylvarus doesn’t normally need any additional incentive to hunt down and slaughter spellcasters and most of them consider it their favorite way of spending time anyway, making such feasts an added bonus at most.

While binding xylvari is extremely difficult due to their formidable spell resistance and a whole array of ways to unbind magic, they can be potent servants indeed and many a wizard tried to bend a xylvarus to his will to set him against a rival. When bartered with, xylvari prefer offerings of spellcasters and spellbooks to destroy, although they drive hard bargains and rarely settle for freshly awakened sorcerers or meager apprentices and their near-empty tomes. Even when cowed into service, a xylvarus will do everything in its power to wiggle its way out of servitude in such a way that will allow it to drain and destroy the arrogant mortal that attempted to coerce the magic eater by magic. Divine casters have a much easier time calling xylvari, as the demons tolerate them better than arcane casters and don’t mind helping them, as long as that help involves hunting their favorite prey.

On their homeplane, xylvari are less domineering and ambitious than many demons, even some less frightening or powerful than them. They rarely gather minions and take charge, preferring a solitary existence and being their own masters or else gaining a place at a powerful demon’s court. For most, working for stronger demons most often boils down to operating as specialized executioners and enforcers, as xylvari are not extraordinarily bright by demon standards and rarely attain high rank.

An average xylvarus is close to 12 feet tall and weighs a gaunt 1000 pounds.
